name: Doeg
bio:
Doeg was an Edomite, the chief of Saul's herdsmen. He happened to be present at Nob when David came to the priest Ahimelech for help (1 Samuel 21:7). Later, when Saul gathered his officials and rebuked them for not telling him of Jonathan's alliance with David, Doeg stepped forward and reported that he had seen David come to Ahimelech at Nob, that Ahimelech had inquired of the LORD for him, given him food, and handed over Goliath's sword (1 Samuel 22:9-10).

Enraged, Saul summoned Ahimelech and all the priests of Nob and ordered them put to death; when Saul's own guards, out of reverence for the LORD's priests, refused to lift a hand against them, Saul turned to Doeg and commanded him to do it. Doeg did not hesitate, killing eighty-five priests wearing the linen ephod that day, then putting the entire town of Nob to the sword — men, women, children, and livestock alike (1 Samuel 22:17-19). Doeg's betrayal and his willing hand in slaughtering an entire town of innocent priests make him one of Scripture's clearest examples of an informer who became an instrument of atrocity; Psalm 52 is traditionally understood as David's response to this very act.
